texts.preamble: Saleha Begum vs The State Of Telangana on 20 September, 2023 Author: K. Lakshman Bench: K. Lakshman Hon'Ble Sri Justice K. Lakshman And Hon'Ble Smt. Justice K. Sujana Writ Petition No.18189 Of 2023 Order:
texts.facts: 2. This writ petition is filed to issue a writ of habeas corpus directing respondent No.3 to produce the detenu viz.,, Mohd. Sohail S/o late Mohd. Abdul Khader, now detained in Central Prison, Chanchalguda, Hyderabad, and [LEAKAGE_MASK] the impugned detention order dated 14.12.2022 passed by respondent No.2 declaring it as illegal. 3. Respondent No.2 passed the detention order dated 14.12.2022 against the detenu under the provisions of Section - 3 (2) of the Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Boot-leggers, Dacoits, Drug-Offenders, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders Land- Grabbers, Spurious Seed Offenders, Insecticide Offenders, Fertilizer Offenders, Food Adulteration Offenders, Fake Document Offenders, KL,J & SKS,J Scheduled Commodities Offenders, Forest Offenders, Gaming Offenders, Sexual Offenders, Explosive Substances Offenders, Arms Offenders, Cyber Crime Offenders and White Collar or Financial Offenders Act, 1986 (Act No.1 of 1986) (for short 'Act No.1 of 1986'), under the category of 'Goonda' as defined under Section - 2 (g) of the Act No.1 of 1986. 4. The impugned detention order was passed by respondent No.2 - detaining authority relying on the following two (02) crimes: Crime No. Offences Allegations levelled Remarks 201/22 of Sec.307 IPC Attempt to kill the victim Conditional bail was Rein Bazar with a knife. PS Charge sheet was filed and CC is awaited. 269/22 of Secs.448 & 386 The detenu trespassed Conditional bail was Rein Bazar Saleha Begum vs The State Of Telangana on 20 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124436292/ 1 IPC and Sec.25 into the house of the granted. PS (1B) of the Arms victim and threatened Charge sheet was filed Act him on the point of knife and the same was to compromise criminal numbered as CC cases filed against him. No.11088 of 2022. 5. The detaining authority while passing the impugned detention order also considered the following two (02) crimes wherein the detenu was involved during the years 2019 and 2021. Crime No. Offences Allegations levelled Remarks 198/18 of Secs.420 & 379 The detenu stolen the The police laid the charge Rein Bazar IPC mobile phone of the sheet and it was numbered PS complainant by diverting as CC 14741/2019 his attention. 250/21 of Sec.354D IPC The detenu harassed the The police laid the charge Rein Bazar and Sec.11 r/w 12 minor girl (14 years) sheet and it was numbered PS of POCSO Act under the guise of love. as SCPCS No.407/2021. KL,J & SKS,J 6. The detaining authority has also referred the past history of detenu in commission of offences in two (02) crimes viz., Crime Nos.198 of 2019 and 250 of 2021. Crime No.250 of 2021 was registered for the offences punishable under Section - 354D of IPC and Section - 11 read with 12 of POCSO Act. In all the said crimes, on completion of investigation, the police laid the charge sheets and the Calendar Cases are pending for trial. . It is mentioned in the impugned detention order dated 14.12.2022 that the detenu has been habitually committing offences including attempt to murder and trespass using dangerous weapons in the limits of Hyderabad Police Commissionerate. He has been causing widespread fear, terror and panic among the general public by committing such offences one after the other after enlarging on bail. After release from judicial custody in Crime No.250 of 2021, there was no change in the attitude of the detenu in commission of offences and he committed the aforesaid crimes viz., Crime No.201 of 2022 and 269 of 2022. Thus, the acts of the detenu would amply demonstrate his habitual nature of committing crimes and causing fear, panic and terror in the minds of general public and make his criminal history evident. 10. The detaining authority further mentioned in the detention order that the detenu is an active and notorious rowdy sheeter and a desperate criminal. It is also apt to refer that the detenu had committed different types of offences, which are grave and serious. In other crime, he has trespassed, threatened the victim with knife. In the past, he has committed theft of mobile phone by diverting the attention of the KL,J & SKS,J victim. He has harassed a 14-year old girl.
texts.arguments: Mr. Pasham Trivikram Reddy, learned counsel for the petitioner, would submit that the impugned detention order was issued without application of mind. The detaining authority did not consider the entire material properly. Therefore, there is no subjective satisfaction by the detaining authority while issuing the impugned detention order. Thus, the detention order is liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. 7. On the other hand, learned Special Government Pleader representing learned Additional Advocate General would submit that the allegations levelled against the detenu are serious and dangerous in nature. The detaining authority considered the entire material placed, satisfied that the activities of the detenu were creating panic and a feeling of insecurity among the general public which were prejudicial to the maintenance of 'public order'. Having felt that the cases registered against him under the ordinary law have no deterrent effect in curbing his prejudicial activities, he is not amenable to ordinary law and with a view to prevent him from further indulging in such prejudicial activities, the detaining authority passed the detention order dated 14.12.2022 and the same was approved vide G.O.Rt.No.2362 of General Administration (Spl. Law & Order) Department, dated 17.12.2022 by respondent No.1. The acts of the KL,J & SKS,J detenu attract under the definition of a 'Goonda' as defined in Clause (g) of Section 2 of the Act No.1 of 1986. Therefore, the detaining authority after arriving at the subjective satisfaction only, passed the detention order. There is no error in it. i) He has also placed reliance on the principle laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Vijay Kumar v. Union of India 1 and Smt. K. Aruna Kumari v. Government of Andhra Pradesh 2. Saleha Begum vs The State Of Telangana on 20 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124436292/ 2 8. 11. Section - 2 (g) of the Act No.1 of 1986 defines "Goonda", which means a person, who either by himself or as a member of or leader of a gang, habitually commits, or attempts to commit or abets the commission of offences punishable under Chapter XVI or Chapter XVII or Chapter XXII of the IPC. 12. Saleha Begum vs The State Of Telangana on 20 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/124436292/ 3 13. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ashok Kumar v. Delhi Administration 3 observed that preventive detention is devised to afford protection to society. The object is not to punish a man for having done something but to intercept before he does it and to prevent him from doing. 14. In Ram Manohar Lohia v. State of Bihar 4, the Apex Court held as under: "...Does the expression "public order" take in every kind of disorder or only some? The answer to this serves to distinguish "public order" from "law and order" because the latter undoubtedly takes in all of them. Public order if disturbed, must lead to public disorder. Every breach of the peace does not lead to public disorder. When two drunkards quarrel and fight there is disorder but not public disorder. They can be dealt with under the powers to maintain law and order but cannot be detained on the ground that they were disturbing public order. Suppose that the two fighters were of rival communities . (1982) 2 SCC 403 . The problem is still one of law and order but it raises the apprehension of public disorder. The contravention of law always affects order but before it can be said to affect public order, it must affect the community or the public at large. It will thus appear that just as "public order" in the rulings of this Court (earlier cited) was said to comprehend disorders of less gravity than those affecting "security of State", "law and order" also comprehends disorders of less gravity than those affecting public order". 15. In Vijay Narain Singh v. State of Bihar 5, a three Judge Bench of the Apex Court had an occasion to deal with the expression 'habitually' and held that the expression 'habitually' would mean 'repeatedly' or 'persistently' implying a thread of continuity, stringing together similar repetitive acts, and a single act or omission would not . The Apex Court was of the opinion that to qualify as a 'habit', a person must have grown accustomed to leading a life of crime, whereby it would be a force of habit, inherent or latent, in an individual with a criminal instinct, with a criminal disposition of mind, that makes him as dangerous to society in general.
